source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Structural Organisation in Animals
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Sponges show the cellular level of organisation because their cells
options: form true tissues with a basement membrane
remain largely independent without forming tissues
are arranged into organs such as a heart
questions.explanation: In Porifera, cells cooperate but do not form true tissues; this is the cellular grade of organisation.

questions.stem: Simple squamous epithelium is typically found in the lining of
questions.explanation: Thin flat cells of simple squamous epithelium favour diffusion in alveoli and capillary walls.

questions.stem: Compound (stratified) epithelium is specialised mainly for
questions.explanation: Several cell layers protect surfaces such as skin and the lining of the mouth from wear.

questions.stem: Adipose tissue stores fat and is a type of
questions.explanation: Adipose and areolar tissues are loose connective tissues with cells in a soft matrix.

questions.stem: Tendons are dense regular connective structures that connect
questions.explanation: Dense regular connective tissue of tendons joins skeletal muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.stem: The flexible skeletal tissue with chondrocytes in lacunae is
questions.explanation: Cartilage is a specialised connective tissue; chondrocytes lie in lacunae within a firm matrix.

questions.stem: Blood is classified as a connective tissue because it has
options: a hard mineral matrix of calcium
cells suspended in a fluid matrix called plasma
questions.explanation: Connective tissues have cells in a matrix; in blood the matrix is plasma.

questions.stem: Unstriated (smooth) muscle is typically found in the wall of the
questions.explanation: Visceral smooth muscle is involuntary and lines hollow organs such as the gut.

questions.stem: Cardiac muscle fibres are characterised by
options: multinucleate peripheral nuclei only, as in skeletal fibres
questions.explanation: Heart muscle is striated, involuntary and joined by intercalated discs for coordinated contraction.

questions.stem: The long process of a neuron that carries the impulse away from the cell body is the
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive signals; a single axon conducts the impulse away from the cyton.

questions.stem: Ciliated columnar epithelium lining the bronchi helps mainly to
questions.explanation: Cilia beat to clear mucus; this epithelium also lines parts of the oviduct.

questions.stem: Haversian systems (osteons) are structural units of
questions.explanation: Mammalian compact bone is organised into osteons with concentric lamellae around a Haversian canal.

questions.stem: Which statement about animal tissues is incorrect?
options: Goblet cells are unicellular glands in columnar epithelium
Ligaments are elastic dense connective tissue joining bone to bone
Skeletal muscle fibres are multinucleate and voluntary
Neuroglia conduct nerve impulses faster than axons
questions.explanation: Neuroglia support and insulate neurons; they do not transmit impulses as axons do.

questions.stem: Platyhelminthes exhibit the tissue level of organisation, whereas annelids show the
questions.explanation: From Annelida onwards, animals typically have organs grouped into organ systems.

questions.stem: Cuboidal epithelium with a brush border of microvilli is found in
options: the inner lining of blood vessels
proximal convoluted tubules of the nephron
questions.explanation: PCT cells are cuboidal with microvilli that increase absorptive surface.

questions.stem: Glandular epithelium is modified mainly for
questions.explanation: Unicellular goblet cells and multicellular glands are epithelial specialisations for secretion.

questions.stem: Areolar tissue contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells in a
options: loose matrix of collagen and elastin fibres
questions.explanation: Loose areolar connective tissue fills spaces and has a semi-fluid matrix with scattered fibres and cells.

questions.stem: Dense irregular connective tissue with fibres oriented in many directions occurs in the
questions.explanation: Dermis has a feltwork of collagen that resists stretch in several planes; tendons have parallel fibres.

questions.stem: Bone differs from cartilage in having
options: a hard matrix rich in calcium salts
no blood supply in living animals
questions.explanation: Bone matrix is calcified and vascular; cartilage matrix is firm but not mineralised like bone.

questions.stem: The most abundant cells in human blood by number are
questions.explanation: Red blood cells far outnumber white cells and platelets in circulating blood.

questions.stem: Skeletal muscle fibres are
options: branched with intercalated discs and involuntary
questions.explanation: Striated skeletal fibres are under voluntary control and have many peripheral nuclei.

questions.stem: Intercalated discs of cardiac muscle
options: attach the heart to the sternum
are cell junctions that allow the fibres to act as a unit
are identical to neuromuscular junctions of the limb
questions.explanation: Gap junctions and desmosomes at intercalated discs couple cardiomyocytes electrically and mechanically.

questions.stem: Nissl's granules in a neuron are composed of
questions.explanation: Nissl bodies are RER plus ribosomes in the cyton and dendrites, absent from the axon hillock and axon.

questions.stem: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) that stretches is a feature of the
questions.explanation: Compound transitional epithelium lines the bladder and ureters and changes shape as the organ fills.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a connective tissue?
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle of the gut is muscular tissue; blood, bone and cartilage are connective tissues.

questions.stem: Match the tissue with an incorrect location or feature.
options: Hyaline cartilage — articular ends of long bones
questions.explanation: Biceps is skeletal (striated voluntary) muscle; smooth muscle occurs in viscera, not in the biceps.
